ranking.note: Raised to P2: privacy/security configuration guidance for a newly merged broadcast feature has more durable user consequence than the other clarification docs, matching the category's 'security and configuration first' rule.
Raised to P4->P3: the current text contradicts actual code (only 58 of 129 LogError calls are fatal, per #30348) and keeps recurring in review debates, i.e. wrong guidance rather than cosmetics.

inconsistencies: #35518 and #35480 (same author) both address parts of issue #14278 on notification semantics; they are complementary, not duplicates, but #35518 should be reviewed first since it establishes the general asynchronous/no-ordering model that the ZMQ-specific guarantees in #35480 sit inside.

#36704 and #36782 are both fanquake comment-hygiene passes touching overlapping source comments; reviewing #36704 first is preferable because it enables the compiler check that would catch regressions of the kind #36782 fixes by hand.
#35858 documents -privatebroadcast, a feature already merged; its content depends on that feature's final option semantics, so any later change to the option must be reflected here.

#36101 and #30361 both aim to settle recurring developer debates about error/logging conventions; #36101 is the broader strategy and is disputed, while #30361 is a narrow factual correction that need not wait on it.
result.notes: The category splits cleanly: one architectural design doc with leverage over other PRs, one privacy/configuration guide, a band of genuinely useful clarification docs for behaviours users and developers trip over, and two comment-hygiene passes with no meaning changes. No PR here corrects documentation that would cause fund loss, so nothing reaches P1.
